### Observed differences

Most of the 84 tested indicators differ only marginally between the windows (occurrence changes of half a point to about four points per 100 traces, transition-mix shifts of a few percentage points); the largest differences are listed below. [OCC005, OCC013, DIR026]

- In the later window, the repeat block A15–A16 runs less often: both activities still appear in every trace, but mean occurrences per trace fell from about 1.8 to about 1.6, traces containing repeats fell from about 44 in 100 to about 35–37 in 100, and the share of A16's outgoing transitions returning to A15 fell from about 44% to about 38%. [OCC014, OCC015, DIR016]
- In the later window, the block A41–A43–A44 runs more often: A43 and A44 take part in about 62 of 100 traces (about 60 before), their mean occurrences rose from about 0.76 to about 0.9 per trace, traces with repeats rose from about 13 to about 20 in 100, and A41 sends about 51% of its outgoing transitions to A43 instead of about 45% (A41→A42 fell from about 52% to about 47%). [OCC035, OCC037, OCC038, DIR041]
- Routing inside the A20–A22–A23 cycle shifted in the later window from back-jumps toward the forward sequence: A20→A22 rose from about 27% to 39% of A20's outgoing transitions while A20→A23 fell from about 40% to 29%; A22→A23 rose from about 22% to 34% while A22→A20 fell from about 39% to 30%; A23→A30 rose from about 30% to 37% while A23→A22 fell from about 37% to 30%; entries via A29→A20 rose from about 28% to 37%. All three activities run in nearly every trace in both windows. [DIR020, DIR022, DIR023, DIR029]
- A08 takes part in about twice as many traces in the later window (about 7 in 100 before, about 16 in 100 after; 14 versus 33 traces), and more distinct outgoing transitions from A08 are observed (13 versus 32). [OCC007, DIR008]
- Smaller shifts in the later window: A24 appears in about 37 of 100 traces (about 30 before), while A19 falls from about 34 to 30 and A06 from about 10 to 8 in 100. [OCC022, OCC018, OCC006]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. Out of 84 indicators only six exceed an empirical strength of 0.9 — no more than the roughly eight extremes expected if the two windows were random splits of one stable process — and those items sit on correlated loop-mates (A15 with A16, A43 with A44, A20 with A22) or on samples of only 10–33 observations, so sampling variability alone can explain every difference listed above. [OCC007, DIR020, DIR022, OCC014, OCC015, DIR002]
